_comment: Catalog-driven SQL rule set for SCOS detection + conversion. Each rule: id, anchor, severity, find (sqlglot exp class for find_all, or '*'), when (declarative predicates, ALL must hold) OR matcher (named predicate in rag.sql_matchers), optional transform (named statement transform), detect (default true), note, optional fixer_action, jira, sources. See rag/sql_engine.py.

rules.note: Window function used in OVER(...) with no ORDER BY; Spark errors, SCOS returns a nondeterministic result. Add an explicit ORDER BY.

rules.anchor: IN (SELECT ...) in LEFT JOIN ON clause
rules.note: An IN (SELECT ...) subquery in a LEFT OUTER JOIN ON clause makes SCOS drop non-matching left rows (INNER semantics). Move the IN predicate into a WHERE clause or a derived table.
rules.fixer_action: Move the IN (SELECT ...) predicate out of the LEFT JOIN ON clause into a WHERE clause or a derived table so SCOS keeps LEFT OUTER semantics.

rules.anchor: SELECT alias collides with column name (LCA)
rules.note: A SELECT output alias reuses the name of a GROUP BY column. Snowflake rejects this with `ambiguous column name`, while Spark resolves it by context. Rename the output alias so it does not shadow a grouped column.
rules.fixer_action: Rename the SELECT output alias so it no longer shadows a GROUP BY column, and update downstream references to the new alias.

rules.note: Multi-column (tuple LHS) NOT IN evaluates NULL-aware anti-join semantics differently in SCOS than Spark. Rewrite as OR'd predicates or a NOT EXISTS anti-join.

INSERT OVERWRITE ... PARTITION(...) on a Snowflake (FDN) table requires `snowpark.connect.sql.emulatePartitionOverwritesForSnowflakeTables=true` in SCOS; without it the partition overwrite is rejected. Enable that config, or use an Iceberg table.
rules.fixer_action: Set spark.conf.set('snowpark.connect.sql.emulatePartitionOverwritesForSnowflakeTables','true') before the statement, or migrate the target to an Iceberg table.

rules.anchor: GROUPING SETS with non-empty GROUP BY
rules.note: SCOS rejects GROUPING SETS combined with a non-empty GROUP BY (and multi-expression ROLLUP/CUBE). The empty-GROUP-BY form is supported. Fold the grouping into the GROUPING SETS list, or UNION ALL per-grain aggregates.
SCOS supports only FLATTEN and SPLIT_TO_TABLE as LATERAL VIEW generators. Rewrite using DataFrame .explode()/.posexplode() or a supported table function.
rules.fixer_action: Rewrite the LATERAL VIEW generator (EXPLODE/POSEXPLODE/INLINE/STACK) using DataFrame .explode()/.posexplode() or a supported table function; qualify the generated columns.

rules.note: SCOS allows at most one table-valued generator (EXPLODE/POSEXPLODE/INLINE/STACK/LATERAL FLATTEN) per SELECT; multiple generators in the same projection raise. Chain successive .select(explode(...)) calls.
rules.fixer_action: Chain successive .select(explode(...)) calls (or LATERAL FLATTEN one array at a time) instead of multiple generators in one projection.

rules.note: SQL TABLESAMPLE has no case in the SCOS relation mapper and is rejected. Use DataFrame .sample(fraction) on the read, or Snowflake SAMPLE via a SnowflakeSession passthrough query.
rules.fixer_action: Use DataFrame .sample(fraction) on the read, or Snowflake SAMPLE via a SnowflakeSession passthrough query, instead of TABLESAMPLE in spark.sql(...).

rules.note: Hive script transform (SELECT TRANSFORM(...) USING 'cmd') is not supported in SCOS. Reimplement the external-script logic as a Snowflake UDF/UDTF or a DataFrame transformation.
rules.fixer_action: Reimplement the TRANSFORM ... USING external-script logic as a Snowflake UDF/UDTF or a DataFrame transformation.

rules.note: Snowflake EXPLAIN covers DML only, so SCOS rejects EXPLAIN over DDL (CREATE/DROP/ALTER/...). Drop the EXPLAIN prefix and run the DDL directly.
SCOS emits a plain Snowflake EXPLAIN for every mode; the mode keyword is silently ignored.
CACHE/UNCACHE TABLE is a no-op on Snowflake/SCOS and may raise; the statement is removed.
SCOS does not support an explicit ROWS/RANGE window frame for this function family (NTH_VALUE, LAST_VALUE, ANY_VALUE, PERCENTILE_DISC/CONT, boolean aggregates, LEAD/LAG, INTERVAL/RANGE bounds).
rules.fixer_action: Remove the explicit window frame (use a plain OVER(PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...)) or compute the value with a supported function; SCOS rejects cumulative/sliding frames for this function.

rules.note: QUALIFY is not in the Spark SQL grammar used by spark.sql(); the SCOS parser (Spark 3.5.3 SparkSqlParser) raises a PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR. Rewrite it as a ROW_NUMBER()-style subquery with an outer WHERE on the window value.

LISTAGG(x, sep) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY y) is rejected by the Spark SQL parser (WITHIN GROUP is not in the grammar) and LISTAGG is not a SCOS function. Rewrite as array_join(array_sort([array_distinct] collect_list(CAST(x AS STRING))), sep). The deterministic rewrite is applied ONLY when WITHIN GROUP orders ascending by the LISTAGG expression itself (array_sort then reproduces the order exactly); a different/DESC/multi-key ORDER BY is left as a residual gap for the LLM fixer to reorder explicitly.
rules.fixer_action: If WITHIN GROUP orders by a column other than the LISTAGG expression (or DESC / multiple keys), reproduce that order explicitly before concatenating — e.g. collect the rows ordered by the key (array of structs sorted by the key, or a windowed/ordered subquery) then array_join — rather than array_sort over the values.

rules.note: The :: cast operator is not in the Spark SQL grammar used by spark.sql() (it is a Spark 4.0 feature); the SCOS parser raises a PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR. It leaves no distinct AST trace, so the engine detects it lexically and regenerates the statement (the spark generator always emits CAST(... AS ...)).

UPDATE <target> SET col = s.col, ... FROM <source> WHERE <conds> (Snowflake join-update) is rejected by the Spark SQL parser — UPDATE has no FROM clause in the grammar (SCOS error 5001). Rewrite as MERGE INTO <target> USING <source> ON <WHERE> WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET .... SCOS supports MERGE (MergeIntoTable). Single-source-table form only; UPDATE ... FROM with joins is left as a residual gap. Multi-match raises a nondeterministic-merge error in Snowflake (vs an arbitrary pick) — equivalent for 1:1/filtered joins.

rules.anchor: CASE expression as a window aggregate
rules.note: A CASE/WHEN expression used as the windowed value (e.g. `CASE WHEN ... THEN MIN(x) ELSE ANY_VALUE(x) END OVER (...)`) is rejected by Snowflake's window resolution — it cannot select the aggregate via a conditional branch. Spark handles it via its plan optimizer. Lift the CASE out of the window (compute each branch's window separately, then CASE over the results).
rules.fixer_action: Move the CASE out of the OVER(...): compute the window for each aggregate branch in its own column, then apply the CASE/WHEN over those windowed columns in an outer projection.

rules.note: Casting an integer/decimal to an INTERVAL type (e.g. `CAST(-122 AS INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH)`) fails in Snowflake; Spark supports it implicitly. SCOS has no translation. Construct the interval explicitly instead of casting a number to it.
rules.fixer_action: Build the interval explicitly from the numeric value (e.g. make_interval / a multiplied INTERVAL literal such as n * INTERVAL '1' MONTH) rather than CAST(<number> AS INTERVAL ...).

rules.note: A `[*]` array wildcard in a JSON path (e.g. `get_json_object(val, '$.store.book[*].category')`) is unsupported — Snowflake's GET_PATH/JSON path accepts only numeric indices. Spark returns the matched array. Rewrite with a LATERAL FLATTEN over the array and project the field per element.
rules.fixer_action: Replace the `[*]` path with a LATERAL FLATTEN over the array (FLATTEN(INPUT => <array>)) and select the target field from each flattened element, or use a UDF to extract the list.

rules.anchor: Correlated scalar subquery with set-op / GROUP BY
rules.note: A correlated scalar subquery whose body contains UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT or a GROUP BY is rejected by Snowflake as an unsupported subquery type (error 002031); Spark evaluates it via its plan optimizer. Candidate — the correlation check is heuristic.
rules.fixer_action: Decorrelate the scalar subquery: rewrite it as a LEFT JOIN to a pre-aggregated (or pre-UNIONed) derived table keyed on the correlation column, then select the aggregated value.

rules.note: IDENTIFIER(...) with a dynamic (non-literal) argument — used to call a table function by computed name or to build object names in DDL. Snowflake's IDENTIFIER() does not support dynamic TVF calls or dynamic object names in CREATE/DROP/ALTER.
rules.fixer_action: Resolve the identifier in Python and emit static SQL, or use a stored procedure / EXECUTE IMMEDIATE for the dynamic object name.

rules.note: map() with a float/decimal, boolean, or timestamp/date key. Snowflake's MAP type only allows VARCHAR or NUMBER(p,0) (integer) keys; Spark allows any hashable key. The map construction fails.
rules.fixer_action: Cast the map key to STRING (or an integer code) before constructing the map — e.g. map(CAST(k AS STRING), v). Note this changes the key type, so verify downstream map lookups.
